- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings — smooth out sharp directional moves; avoid large jumps in 30d forecast unless sentiment confirms sustained trend.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak or rises after trough), model often fails to correct — apply downward bias after peaks, upward bias after troughs.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: model tends to be too optimistic in early days, then corrects — consider smoothing forecast curve to match recent sentiment and price momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend, not just magnitude.
